description: The line plot illustrates the maximum activation values across 22 neural network layers for four distinct components: attn_output, attn_residual, ffn_output, and ffn_residual, as labeled in the legend. The x-axis, labeled “Layer,” spans from 0 to 22 with integer tick marks at every 5 units, representing discrete layer indices in a transformer-style architecture. The y-axis, labeled “Max Activation Value,” ranges from 0 to 1600 with major tick marks at intervals of 200, indicating the peak activation magnitude observed per layer for each component. The attn_output (blue dashed line) remains near zero across all layers, with a slight rise to approximately 200 at layer 22. The attn_residual (orange dotted line) exhibits a sharp spike to ~1400 at layer 5, remains elevated around 1500–1600 until layer 21, then drops sharply to ~400 at layer 22. The ffn_output (green dash-dotted line) shows a brief spike to ~1400 at layer 5, drops to near zero until layer 13, spikes again to ~1000 at layer 14, then declines to near zero until layer 21, followed by a sharp rise to ~1200 at layer 22. The ffn_residual (red solid line) mirrors the attn_residual’s trajectory closely, peaking at ~1400 at layer 5, staying high (~1500–1600) until layer 21, then falling to ~400 at layer 22. All lines exhibit sparse, transient activation patterns with pronounced peaks at specific layers, consistent with the paper’s focus on sparsity and non-linearity in attention mechanisms.
